findings.title: Mutex guards only the cache pointer, not the shared EntryPointAssets object handed to callers
findings.body: The new RWMutex protects reads/writes of the `entryPointAssetsCache` variable, but in non-Dev mode `GetWebAssets` still returns the *same* `*dtos.EntryPointAssets` instance to every concurrent request. That type is mutable: it has exported fields (`JSFiles`, `Dark`, `Light`) and a mutating method `SetContentDeliveryURL`. If any caller (now or in the future) mutates the returned value — e.g. calls `SetContentDeliveryURL` or appends to `JSFiles` — that write races with all other goroutines reading the same object, reproducing exactly the class of bug this PR is meant to fix. To fully close the race, return a copy of the cached value, or make the DTO immutable.

findings.title: No cache re-check after acquiring the write lock; lock held across file I/O and JSON parsing
findings.body: Once a goroutine that observed a nil cache acquires the exclusive lock, it never re-checks whether another goroutine has already populated the cache. At startup (or after a failed read, when the cache stays nil), N concurrent requests each perform the full manifest read and JSON decode sequentially while holding the write lock, instead of one goroutine doing it and the rest reusing the result. Additionally, the lock is held across `os.Open` + `json.Decode` and, in Dev mode, this happens on every single request, serializing all index-page requests behind each other's disk I/O. Doing the expensive computation first and only taking the lock to publish the result (double-checked locking) would avoid the redundant work and shrink the critical section.

findings.title: No regression test for the fixed data race
findings.body: The PR fixes a data race on shared global state but adds no test that would have caught it, so a future refactor could silently reintroduce it. A small test calling `GetWebAssets` concurrently from several goroutines (run under `go test -race`) would lock the fix in, and would also fail on the pre-PR code, demonstrating the bug.
